title: Lawyers question ICC limits on victim participation
summary: The legal representatives of victims in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte have opposed the possibility of further limits to victim participation in the ongoing…

blocks.text: Undated photo shows facade of the International Criminal Court in the Hague, Netherlands.

MANILA, Philippines — The legal representatives of victims in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte have opposed the possibility of further limits to victim participation in the ongoing proceedings at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

In a 19-page response and request for clarification dated Nov. 17, the Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV) urged the Trial Chamber III not to adopt a new interpretation of who can participate in the case.
The filing was in response to the Oct. 29 report submitted by the ICC Registry, which presented an updated scope of the Duterte trial based on a recent decision of the trial judges.

Under the adjusted scope, the case will only cover alleged murders committed in Davao City between 2013 and around June 2016, alleged murders of “high-value targets” between around July 2016 and July 2017, and alleged murders and attempted murders in barangay clearance operations between around July 2016 and September 2018.
If applied, the adjusted scope would exclude at least 13 applications or 16 victims previously allowed to participate in the case, the Registry said.

These include alleged murders committed in Davao City between Nov. 1, 2011 and Dec. 31, 2012, those committed “around Davao City” during the period, and the alleged murders and attempted murders after September 2018.
